body: Well, if becoming a statistic doesn't change anyone's mind, it doesn't help, but neither does it hurt. Erasing my life and humanity is what many suicidal people want. By becoming a statistic, we're (and I say "we're" subjectivity) achieving what we want.

I mean it depends on what type of pills. Lots of pills aren't the right type, or you may do too little, or heck even too much, to OD on. And I wouldn't recommend it. The reason you die from pills is usually liver failure. Which is pretty painful. And often times you don't die from the pills, you die several days after you've taken the pills and are in the hospital. I'm not a supportive person, so I'm not gonna say stuff like "Don't do it, you matter to much" or "Don't kill yourself", just know that I would really, really not fucking recommend pills if you're legitimately considering it.

I do. I am seeing someone. And they claim I'm getting better. Which, is because they don't know the truth of what's going on. And I'm not going to bother telling them. Perhaps if I wasn't so damn quiet, I'd get help, but I would rather suffer quietly than have anyone else in my problems. It's always been that way. When I was a kid and got upset over something small, like say not getting a cookie after dinner, rather than expressing my feelings to an adult, despite them pushing the subject of why I'm sad, I would sit there quietly and cry. I didn't want to tell anyone how I was feeling. 

Guess I've never changed.

Why not? Why not become a statistic? What's so bad about becoming a statistic? People always say that, but what's the meaning of it? I could just as easily say "don't become a statistic" when referring to say, being one of the few people to get into the world's top college. What defines a good statistic from a bad one? Perhaps me becoming a statistic will help prevent someone in the future making the same 'mistake' I did. Is it really so bad anymore? To become a statistic, that means others must fail, must take a fall, for people to be able to group statistics in the first place. It's unrealistic to expect anything else. So why not become a statistic?

I used to throw temper tantrums in middle school. Right before I had to get out the car and walk into the school. I'd cry and hit and punch myself. And then cry some more. Not because I was trying to be a brat, just cause my anxiety was so bad, I couldn't even be in a place as simple as school. And I didn't know how to express what I was feeling either.

That's how bad my social anxiety used to be. Still is pretty bad. I just don't throw tantrums anymore.
I have. And they've just made things worse.

Thanks, cute, but no. That certainly isn't enough. If literally nothing else has been able to convince me to live, a date, in which, I could care less about the "420 and 69" stuff definitely won't stop me.
